utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Klar, ich bin dabei. Sag mir kurz, was noch fehlt.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Mir fehlt noch etwas Material und ein paar Hände für morgen. Ich schicke dir gleich die genaue Liste.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Alles klar, schick mir die Liste, dann plane ich morgen mit.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I can help, but I need to know the schedule and where the repairs are happening so I can plan the drive.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I can help, but I still need the schedule and repair locations to plan the drive.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right, the repair drive. I must’ve missed the update, but I’m here now.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Glad you made it, Noah. We’re just getting started, so you haven’t missed much.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Good, I’m glad I didn’t miss the actual start.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I’ll bring it up with Ira and keep the repair drive moving.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Good to hear. Let me know what I can do to help with it.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Absolutely, I’ll check in with Ira and keep you posted on what’s needed.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sorry I’m late — how’s the repair drive coming along?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Pretty well so far — we’ve got a decent pile of finished fixes, and I’m still sorting the last few jobs.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Glad to hear it’s going well. Need another hand with the last few jobs?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: I’d like to keep it simple: what’s the plan, and when do you want me to bring my part over?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Keep it simple: bring your part by Saturday afternoon, and I’ll line everything up at the driveway then.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Saturday afternoon works for me. I’ll bring my part then.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: What exactly needs fixing on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Mostly the loose fence boards, the broken gate latch, and a couple of porch steps that need re-securing.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Got it. How many people are we expecting to help with it?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: I can round up a few more folks if you need hands for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: That'd help a lot. I’m tracking the houses that still need a hand, so send them my way.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Perfect, I’ll send over the folks I’ve got and keep an eye out for anyone else who can pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: I can help with that, Rosa. Tell me what needs fixing and I’ll see what I can do.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Great, Mara. I’ll send over the list this afternoon, and we can start with the porch steps and the loose fence gate.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Absolutely, send the list this afternoon and I’ll get started on the porch steps and the gate.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’ve got a few spare tarps and a roll of duct tape if that helps the drive.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Nice, those will help. I’ll grab the tarp and tape if you can bring them by.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Perfect, I’ll bring the tarp and tape by soon.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: I heard they’re still gathering tools for the repair drive down on Maple, and by the looks of it they could use a few more hands.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Yeah, and I heard they’re hoping for folks who can haul, sort, or just lend a steady pair of hands. I’m thinking of stopping by after lunch.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Can you tell me what still needs fixing on the repair drive? I want to make sure I have the details right before I help.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Sure, tell me the specific things that still need fixing, and I’ll keep track of them carefully.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it, I’ll take a quick look and be there.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Thanks, I’ll watch for you.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: On my way now.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Yeah, I can help with the repair drive. I’ll keep spreading the word.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Thanks, Vik. I’ll check in with the rest of the neighbors and keep the repair drive moving.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Absolutely, I’ll keep spreading the word and check back in with you soon.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right — the repair drive. I might’ve missed a change; what do I need to know?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I think it’s still on for Saturday. I can send you the details if you want.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Sure, send me the details.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can help with that if you want to walk me through what needs fixing.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Absolutely — point me to the first thing that needs attention and I’ll help sort it out.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Sure, show me the first thing on the list and I’ll help with it.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Absolutely, I can keep track of the sign-ups and make sure the repair drive stays organized.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Rosa. I’ll keep an eye on the locations and make sure we know where everything is going.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That sounds great, Opal. I’ll keep everything lined up on my end, and we’ll make sure the drive runs smoothly.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I can help, but I need to know the schedule and where the parts are going first.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Sure — I’ll send over the schedule and label the parts drop-off spot so you know exactly where they’re going.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That works, as long as I get the schedule before anything starts moving.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: You mean the repair drive is actually happening today, right?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Yes, that’s right — today, unless something changed. Have you heard any new details?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Okay, I just wanted to make sure. What time is everyone meeting?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Let’s keep it simple: tell me what’s broken and what you need moved.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I’ve got a couple things that need moving, and I’ll tell you the broken parts once I’m sure what’s already on hand.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Just tell me what’s broken when you know, and I’ll keep the moving list ready.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I just heard there’s a repair drive going on. What do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: We need screws, wood glue, and a hammer if you’ve got one. I can use any extra wire or tape too.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I can bring those over, and I’ll check whether I’ve got any tape or wire too.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right, the repair drive. I meant to ask Mara which house needed the most help first.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: The cottage by the corner needs the most help first; its porch is leaning worst.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Got it, I’ll help with the porch first.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can swing by after school pickup, but I need the timing nailed down first. What window works for you?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: I can do 4:15 to 4:45. If that works, I’ll be there at 4:15.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: 4:15 works for me. I’ll plan on being there right at 4:15.
